finding.summary: The findings extraction assumes every file in state.values['files'] has a corresponding entry in results. If the checkpoint is corrupted, from a different graph version, or the graph logic has a bug, this will raise a KeyError. The graph's after_review logic should ensure all files have results when state.next is empty, but there's no defensive check.
finding.fix: Use results.get(f, {}).get('issues', []) to safely handle missing entries, or add an assertion that all files have results before extraction.

label: false_positive
label_reason: the adapter only reads results after checking the graph reached END (state.values and not state.next); after_review routes to report only when every file in files has a result, so results[f] exists for each.
